annotation.title_clean: Trust regulation in Social Robotics: From Violation to Repair
annotation.title_en: Trust regulation in Social Robotics: From Violation to Repair
annotation.venue: CHI EA '23 (SARs: TMI workshop), ACM / arXiv
annotation.summary_en: Short CHI workshop paper reporting a within-subject Wizard-of-Oz experiment with a small humanoid robot in a collaborative game. It tests five trust calibration strategies (proficiency, situation awareness, transparency, violation, repair) and finds they significantly shift measured trust. It contains no governance provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trust in a social robot can be manipulated and regulated within a single interaction.
Trust violation lowered, and an apology-based repair restored, perceived trust (ANOVA p<0.001).
A robot showing situation awareness was rated significantly more benevolent than baseline.
Calibrated trust is needed to avoid over-trust and under-trust in human-robot teams.
Small sample: 14 analysed participants out of 24.
